recipes.name: Strawberry Rhubarb Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 pound rhubarb, cut into 1/4 inch slices
1 (14.1 ounce) package pastry for a double crust 9-inch pie

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Mix flour and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add strawberries and chopped rhubarb. Toss with sugar and flour and let stand for 30 minutes.
Pour filling into prepared pie crust. Dot top with butter, and cover with top crust. Seal edges of top and bottom crust with water.
Brush egg yolk on top of pie with a pastry brush.
Cut several slits in the top crust to allow steam to escape.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and brown, about 35 to 40 minutes. Cool pie on rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Rhubarb Pie
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry rhubarb pie has a ruby-red filling with a delicious sweet-tart flavor in a buttery crust to make a sensational springtime dessert.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a classic rhubarb and strawberry pie. For centuries, this fresh and tangy dessert has been a favorite in spring and summer. Enjoy the sweet-tart flavor of strawberry rhubarb pie filling, baked in your favorite homemade or frozen pie crust. Pair this pie with vanilla ice cream for a dessert that is perfect for picnics, dinner parties, or a sunny afternoon!

review.reviewBody: This is a very simple and very yummy recipe. For those who found the pie too runny but don't want to go through the hassle of pre-cooking the rhubarb, try using a lattice top instead of the double crust called for in the recipe. It lets alot of the moisture out. Also, be sure to let the filling sit the whole 30 min before pouring into crust, and let the pie sit in the oven 15-20 min after baking (oven should be turned OFF) to let the excess fluids thicken. If you do all of those steps, the pie won't be runny, nor will it taste floury.

I've made this pie twice, first as written & the second time I made some changes. Using flour, the pie was runny & tasted like flour. So, the second time, I put the rhubarb in a large pot, added the sugar & 1/4 to 1/2 cup of water with 2 Tablespoons of corn starch dissolved in the water. I cooked it until it thickened. I removed the pot from the stove & added the raw strawberries. I poured the mixture into the crust & dotted with butter. It turned out much better with the cornstarch. Not too much liquid & no flour taste. Also, I just brush the top crust with milk & sprinkle with some sugar & nutmeg.

This was amazing! I went strawberry picking yesturday and made the pie today along with local fresh rhubarb. i changed the recipe by using 3 cups each of strawberries and rhubarb. i didn't use the flour but instead (as previously mentioned) mixed 1/4 cup of water with 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and let it sit with the berries, rhubarb and sugar for 30 minutes. i also baked the pie for 15 minutes at 425 and then 40 minutes at 375. we let the pie cool for about 3-4 hours and it's not runny at all!! this was so good that i'm making 2 more of these pies to give to my family and neighbor! also just a note - you don't need to cook the rhubarb before hand - you need to make sure it's chopped up (about 1/4 inch) and also if you notice the skin is a little tough, peel it a little bit. thanks so much for a recipe that i'll definitely use again and again!!

I have made this recipe five times and it is now a favorite in my home! For those that don’t want to go by lbs and pints— I use three cups of quartered strawberries and three cups of sliced rhubarb. For those complaining about the pie being runny— I bake it at 375 for 25 min with foil covering the outer edge of the crust, then remove the foil and bake it for another 25-30 mins until the filling is nice and bubbly. It’s also important to let the pie cool for at least 3 hours so the filling can set. I’ve never had it be runny at all. For me, whenever I bake a fruit/berry pie lowering the temp and baking it longer helps the fruit to cook down and set properly. Make this pie, you will love it!!!

Flavor of the filling was great. I adjusted the cooking temp and time to 1 hr 40 min at 375. Double crust fruit pies need much more time than most think. I believe these changes would solve all the issues the people who gave bad reviews had. I also used raw sugar instead of white on top. Will make again

Wow, this is phenomenal. Used freshly picked, locally grown strawberries which were really juicy. I added a couple tablespoons of tapioca which eliminated any concern over a runny filling. I let it cool for about 3 hours, and it was absolutely perfect. The combination of the tartness of the rhubarb and the sweetness of the strawberries produced one of the best pies I've ever had.*****UPDATE 6.4.19 I make t his pie annually, only once during rhubarb season, and this recipe simply never lets me down. It's my husband's favorite pie (well, second to apple, maybe).

This is a good basic recipe but I added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and the grates zest of one lemon. Instead of the flour I added 1/3 cup of tapioca plus a tablespoon to 3 1/2 cups quartered strawberries, 4 cups rhubarb( half frozen, half fresh) and 1 1/4 cups sugar and 1/4 c. brown sugar. My strawberries were not very sweet . I mixed the rhubarb, strawberry, sugar and tapioca, zest and cinnamon together and let it marinate while I rolled out the dough. I chilled the dough for 10 minutes then added the fruit and put a lattice top on the fruit. I covered the edge with foil and baked on bottom rack of oven at 425 F degree oven for 15 minutes then transferred pie to foil lined cookie sheet , lowered oven temp to 350 and baked until crust was browned and bubbly.

I used 1/2 cup of sugar instead of a cup, because I wanted the rhubarb to stay sour and I really don’t like too much sugar in my fruit pies (or sugar on fruit, in general). My taste tester thought it was perfect but I would like even less sugar. Added about a 1/2 cup of blueberries. Added two tbsp. of Bob’s Red Mill 1-to-1 Gluten Free flour to the sugar and fruit mixture to thicken it. I also put a half teaspoon each of of vanilla extract and almond extract in the fruit mixture. In the future, I would lower that to about 1/2 or 1/4 of a teaspoon each. The crust/topping is the only thing I’d have changed and that wasn’t this recipe’s fault (I’m still trying to perfect my gluten free pie crust). I baked it for about 20 minutes longer than the recipe said. It has a very delicious rhubarb flavor and the strawberry is very pronounced. My taste tester liked it and doesn’t even care for strawberry rhubarb. I’ll definitely be making this again this summer.

I made this for Thanksgiving! My grandpas favorite pie is strawberry rhubarb. I took a few suggestions (like buying frozen cut rhubarb at Sprouts). I mostly followed the recipe and didn’t pre-cook anything. I rinsed the frozen rhubarb and weeded out the larger thicker looking chunks. Tossed it with the strawberries then tossed them with the sugar and flour, AND LET SIT FOR THE FULL 30 MINUTES. I did alter cooking to 15 minutes at 425 and then 350 for 40 minutes, and had the crust edge covered until the last 15 minutes. I did the egg/sugar on the crust... and I did sprinkle cinnamon and nutmeg over the topping before placing the upper crust since it’s fall. I followed the suggestion of doing lattice to allow steam out, I also baked it the night before and didn’t cut it for near 24 hours. It was PERFECT!!! No flour flavor, rhubarb was all soft and tangy (not sour), and the pie held together while being cut and served! I’m so happy, will definitely be doing this one again!
After reading other reviews, I was nervous about the filling being too runny; so I added a little bit of cornstarch to the sugar/flour mixture and baked the pie for 1 hour at 375. It was delicious!

I made it as written. I would suggest 2 1/2 cups of cut up strawberries and the same for the cut up rhubarb. I did let it stand for nearly an hour in the sugar/flour mixture (by accident) and poured off some the liquid off before placing the fruit into the pie plate. I read one review that said to turn off the oven at the end of the baking period and leave the pie in the overnight for 15 minutes. It was delicious! Not runny at all.
Oh my is this ever good! Fresh picked rhubarb & strawberries. Slap your momma good!

This was quite possibly the best pie I've ever made. And it wasn't runny at all. I followed the recipe exactly, except I baked it for much longer than stated until the internal temperature of the middle of the pie hit 205-210°F. That's how you know a fruit pie is done. From there, I let it cool for three hours, which you also have to do for a fruit pie to set. It was still somewhat warm but not runny. This pie is the perfect balance between sweet and sour and I will be making this many more times in the future. Yum! Thank you!
It tastes fine but it's too wet! After all that work....I was pretty disappointed with the finished product.

Tasted really good! The pie set as it was supposed to, used cast iron skillet since I didn't have a regular pie pan. Didn't do the egg wash or sugar on top. Used fresh rhubarb from the garden and used some strawberries that I had in the freezer (thawed). Would definitely make again!
Simple and easy - maximum results for minimum effort. I wait for the height of strawberry season and make an all butter crust. Always amazing!

Delicious old fashioned recipe. The key to fruit pies is to let it rest 3-4 hours at room temp before slicing to avoid a runny pie. Back in the day, there were pie cabinets with screens in kitchens for this purpose! I skipped egg on top and wiped with a moist paper towel for sugar sprinkles.
This was super easy to make and the sweet and sour mingled so nicely. Very tasty especially with vanilla ice cream on top.
Yummy, i forgot to sprinkle the sugar on top tho
Very simple but missing more time due to the bottom dough being not done and too watery of result. Read the comments!!
